e-8203.knowledge_point: Computing the Probability of a Normal Random Variable on an Unbounded Interval
e-8203.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

$$
P(X <       x) = P \left( Z <       \dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma} \right)
$$

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = 2$ and $\sigma = 2.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<1.24) & =P(Z<\frac{1.24-2}{2}) \\  & =P(Z<-0.38) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.38) \\  & =Φ(-0.38)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/48d92806543cb86b2906032b1723fa942db842e7f283681cafeeb9b11fca8cab.png)

According to the table, we have

$$
\Phi(-0.38) = 0.3520.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(X <               1.24) = 0.3520.
$$

e-8204.knowledge_point: Computing the Probability of a Normal Random Variable on an Unbounded Interval Using the Complement
e-8204.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $Y \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

$$
P(Y \geq y) = P \left( Z \geq \dfrac{y-\mu}{\sigma} \right)
$$

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = 5$ and $\sigma = 4.$

First, we transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 2.92) & =P(Z\ge \frac{2.92-5}{4}) \\  & =P(Z\ge -0.52)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/049e4733082674668ebbe2c5a710cd847f1db16d26fdcd2af6e603941efdffe7.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -0.52) & =1-P(Z<-0.52) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -0.52) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.52)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we know that

$$
\Phi(-0.52) =0.3015.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z\ge -0.52) & =1-Φ(-0.52) \\  & =1-0.3015 \\  & =0.6985.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(Y \geq 2.92) = 0.6985.
$$

e-8205.knowledge_point: Computing the Probability of a Normal Random Variable on a Bounded Interval
e-8205.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2),$ we have

$$
P(a <        X <        b) = P \left( \dfrac{a-\mu}{\sigma} <        Z <        \dfrac{b-\mu}{\sigma} \right)
$$

where $Z \sim N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu = 1$ and $\sigma = \sqrt 9 = 3.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.13<X<3.25) & =P(\frac{-1.13-1}{3}<Z<\frac{3.25-1}{3}) \\  & =P(-0.71<Z<0.75)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/a50513f550d8a3122e2f2276883a0189fe9bdc6dd19159e8ae94dbd5b247f5a9.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.71<Z<0.75) & =P(Z<0.75)-P(Z\le -0.71) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.75)-P(Z\le -0.71) \\  & =Φ(0.75)-Φ(-0.71)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.71) & =0.2389 \\ Φ(0.75) & =0.7734\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.71<Z<0.75) & =Φ(0.75)-Φ(-0.71) \\  & =0.7734-0.2389 \\  & =0.5345.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(-1.13<          X <          3.25) = 0.5345.
$$

P(a<X<b)=P(a−μσ<Z<b−μσ)

where Z∼N(0,1) is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have μ=−5 and σ=16=4.

P(0.64<X<3.64)=P(0.64−54<Z<3.64−54)=P(−1.09<Z<−0.34)

Finally, we conclude that

P(0.64<X<3.64)=0.2290.

content.worked_solution:
Given a normal random variable $X∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),$ we have

$$
P(a<X<b)=P(\frac{a-\mu }{\sigma }<Z<\frac{b-\mu }{\sigma })
$$

where $Z∼N(0,1)$ is a standard normal random variable. In our case, we have $\mu =-5$ and $\sigma =\sqrt{16}=4.$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.64<X<3.64) & =P(\frac{0.64-5}{4}<Z<\frac{3.64-5}{4}) \\  & =P(-1.09<Z<-0.34)\end{aligned}
$$

The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070250/assets/6c919bfe71b67ed94751cb53bd5f24e9e80e7979a28a8e28b123aac907d6b7e4.png)

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.09<Z<-0.34) & =P(Z<-0.34)-P(Z\le -1.09) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.34)-P(Z\le -1.09) \\  & =Φ(-0.34)-Φ(-1.09)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.34) & =0.3669 \\ Φ(-1.09) & =0.1379\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.09<Z<-0.34) & =Φ(-0.34)-Φ(-1.09) \\  & =0.3669-0.1379 \\  & =0.2290.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(0.64<X<3.64)=0.2290.
$$
